thread:
Sam: Quick heads-up — canary for /v2/generate (promo-campaign) showing ~2% of responses where `metadata` is completely absent rather than null. Some downstream code in our JS SDK treats absent vs null differently and a few internal customers hit an uncaught error.

Maria: Are those responses valid per the schema? I thought `metadata` was optional. If optional, absent is fine.

Kevin: Schema is `metadata?: object` (optional). Current rule was: omit optional fields when not applicable. But I know older internal clients expect `metadata: null` explicitly.

Samira: Confirming from canary logs: content-type header is `application/json; charset=utf-8`. Payload looks like:
```json
{"id":"gen_123","text":"Hello","score":0.92}
```
so no `metadata` key at all.

Sam: Right — this causes the JS SDK (auto-destructuring code) to do `const { metadata } = resp` then `metadata.source` -> crash. It's an easy fix in app code, but we should decide platform behavior to avoid breaking customers.

Maria: Options I see: (A) keep omitting optional fields and tell SDKs to normalize (recommended long-term), (B) platform adds `metadata: null` by default for backward compat, (C) add feature flag per-route to toggle.

Kevin: From infra side, adding nulls is cheap. But I'd rather enforce a single convention. Our typed clients (pydantic models) raise ValidationError if a field is required; for optional they accept missing. Problem is language inconsistencies — JS devs often expect keys present.

Samira: Proposed short-term: ship SDK patch that normalizes missing->null for selected endpoints and add a server-side canary switch to emit explicit nulls for 48h so we can monitor. Long-term: document convention and update examples to avoid implicit property access.

Maria: I'm +1 for that sequencing. Can we scope to promo-campaign first? We should avoid global change until we audit other endpoints.

Sam: I'll open an SDK PR. Plan:
- SDK: normalizeMissingFields behavior behind a flag (default off)
- Server: add `emit_null_for_missing` canary flag for /v2/generate (promo-campaign)
- Roll canary for 48h, monitor `client_error` and `sdk_normalized_count` metrics

Kevin: I'll add the canary flag to the hosted config and wire a metric (`null_emission_active` + count emitted).

Samira: For the PR, include a small test showing BEFORE and AFTER:
```js
// before
const resp = { id: 'gen_1', text: 'x' }
console.log(resp.metadata.source) // crash

// after (sdk normalizes)
const resp = normalize(resp)
console.log(resp.metadata) // null
```

Sam: Pinged on my PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/842 (WIP). Can reviewers please prioritize? Tagging @Maria @Kevin.

DeployBot: Canary rollout scheduled: promo-campaign /v2/generate -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% over 1 hour if no errors > 0.5%

Maria: Approved for canary. SDK team — please cut the patch today, we'll monitor.

Kevin: I added alerting on `500` spikes and an ad-hoc dashboard showing `responses_with_missing_metadata` vs `responses_with_null_metadata`.

Samira: Also note: we should update our example schema in the docs to clearly show the optional field rule and a snippet on handling missing fields in client code. I'll draft a short blurb.

Sam: Thanks all. I'll post a short follow-up with rollout timestamps and the PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
